_README: Shared cases for the two POI id resolvers (#831, features/POI_IDENTITY.md section 4).
There is one resolver per runtime and there has to be: the pipeline is not
importable from the client, and a phone gets the published tombstones rather
than the ledger. This file is what holds the two implementations to the same
the same ones through resolvePoiId. A case added here is a case both must pass.
`ledger` is the pipeline's view: every row, live and retired. The client's view
is derived from it in the test - tombstones are the rows carrying `retired`,
and everything else is live - because deriving it is what proves the client
sees the same world through a smaller artifact rather than a different one.
A row is `{}` for live, or carries `retired` and optionally `superseded_by`.
Nothing else here is read: name, position and source belong to the card, not

cases.name: a live id resolves to itself
a superseded tombstone resolves to its survivor
cases.why: The whole point of the edge: a hiker's photos follow it home.

cases.name: a place merged twice over two refreshes still arrives somewhere
a retired id with no successor resolves to nothing
cases.why: The honest answer, not a failure: this place is gone and nothing took its place. Every one of the 93 real tombstones is this case today.

cases.name: an id this ledger has never held resolves to nothing
cases.why: A reference from somewhere this project cannot vouch for. Inventing a target would be worse than saying so.

cases.name: a cycle returns nothing rather than hanging
cases.why: reconcile_poi_identity cannot write one, but a hand-edited merged_into override can, and a frozen app is a bad way to learn that.

cases.name: a chain ending in a tombstone with no successor resolves to nothing
cases.why: The successor was itself retired later and nothing replaced it. Following the edge to a dead end is not the same as stopping at the first hop.

cases.name: an edge pointing at an id neither live nor retired resolves to nothing
cases.why: export_retired_poi refuses to publish this, so it can only come from a hand-edited ledger - and both resolvers have to survive one.

cases.name: a source swap keeps the id and does not change the answer
cases.why: features/POI_IDENTITY.md section 5: tier 2 carries an opentrail_at id onto an ATC-sourced row. The id's prefix is history; the resolver never reads it.
